claims.explanation: Lapatinib is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 tyrosine kinase inhibitor, so selective killing is best explained by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling, most clearly through ERBB2 amplification/overexpression or activating EGFR mutations. The sensitive lines include EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) and HER2/ERBB2-driven contexts such as ZR751 breast cancer, while many resistant lines lack these dependencies. Additional modifiers such as PTEN loss/PIK3CA mutation may tune downstream PI3K-AKT dependence, but the primary predictive features are ERBB2 expression/amplification and EGFR mutation/expression.

features.basis: lapatinib targets ERBB2; HER2-positive breast cancer is the approved setting
activating EGFR mutations predict EGFR TKI response; EGFR-mutant lung lines are among the most killed
lapatinib directly inhibits EGFR; EGFR-driven lines should be more sensitive
ERBB2 alterations can activate the lapatinib target pathway
PTEN loss may increase PI3K-AKT dependence downstream of ERBB2/EGFR; seen in sensitive ZR751 and FTC133
PIK3CA pathway activation may cooperate with ERBB2/EGFR blockade; seen in several sensitive lines
KRAS mutations drive ERBB-independent MAPK signaling and are common in resistant lines
BRAF mutations activate MAPK downstream of ERBB and are common in resistant melanoma/colorectal lines
NRAS mutations bypass ERBB dependence; seen in resistant lines
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK independent of ERBB; seen in resistant lines
MET amplification/overexpression can bypass ERBB2 inhibition; HGC27 is resistant and MET-mutant
MEK activation downstream of ERBB can confer resistance; NCIH1437 is resistant and MAP2K1-mutant
